2637: #### 8.5.6 Imports, the linked prelude, and the frontend catalog (phase C4)
2638: 
2639: This section records the C4 design as amended by the C4 cross-ruling's
2640: nineteen converged rulings; where they differ from the design's own
2641: recommendations, the converged rulings govern. Its implementation is
2642: pending, in slices F2, F3, P1 to P3, and I1 to I7 below; F1, P1 and P2
2643: have landed; P2 covers the semantic, stack and register VMs, the walker
2644: waiting on L-b.
2645: 
2646: Install delivers code; instantiation is the importing task's own
2647: evaluation (ruling 1). A linked Python-side module (the base prelude,
2648: the hook prelude, any Python module) exports only closures and immutable
2649: specification data. Its install child defines lambdas and halts. Python
2650: namespaces, class objects, hook state, and runtime cells are allocated
2651: later by an explicit initialization in the consuming task. This is
2652: section 8.5.1's "the linker delivers content-addressed code images,
2653: never Python namespaces" taken literally. Running a module body inside
2654: the install child fails four ways against the landed linker:
2655: 
2656: - The lift refuses. A heap cell ref is non-portable, and every Python
2657:   function, class, dict, and module is a cell, so no body-executed
2658:   module could reach `linked`.
2659: - Output vanishes. Import-time `print` writes the child's output, which
2660:   is never published.
2661: - Identities duplicate. The child lowers its own copy of each
2662:   dependency, so builtin classes in the export slice would be fresh cells
2663:   and `isinstance` would fail.
2664: - First link wins. The parent discards the child's writes to a
2665:   dependency's store.
2666: 
2667: So C4 needs no heap-slice lift, and nothing is copied per receiving task
2668: (section 8.5.1, amended). `py/init!` initializes the prelude's own
2669: active module store once, idempotently, with defined failure behavior;
2670: entry wrappers call it and install children never do. An imported body
2671: runs under the importing task's declared effects and may itself suspend:
2672: "no code-delivery wait inside `py/import`" is not a promise that body
2673: execution cannot park.
2674: 
2675: Module shape. A Python unit compiled as module `a.b` becomes one linker
2676: module:
2677: 
2678: ```clojure
2679: (do (require 'py)              ; hoisted: code delivery only
2680:     (require 'pym.c)           ; one per static import in the unit
2681:     (yin/def spec {:name "a.b" :package? false})
2682:     (yin/def body (fn [%globals %globals-fn] <lowered module body>)))
2683: ;; :yin.module/exports #{spec body}
2684: ```
2685: 
2686: - Hoisted, pinned requires are an explicit eager-dependency restriction,
2687:   not an invisible transformation (ruling 4). `if False: import
2688:   missing`, a caught failed import, and a pre-populated `sys.modules`
2689:   all tell it apart from Python's statement-time import, and the support
2690:   profile says so. The required module names are derivable from rows;
2691:   their manifest addresses additionally need the pinned resolution
2692:   snapshot.
2693: - Body execution stays lazy. `import c` lowers at the statement to
2694:   `(py/import "c" pym.c/spec pym.c/body)` plus the binding, and the body
2695:   runs in the importing task, in statement order.
2696: - `__package__` comes from `spec`: package-ness is source layout, not
2697:   derivable from rows.
2698: 
2699: Names (ruling 3). The registry nests dotted names, so a module `a`
2700: presumably shadows `a.b` (inferred by the design, untested). Until the
2701: linker seat fixes that, no linker module name is a dotted prefix of
2702: another:
2703: 
2704: ```text
2705: +---------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
2706: | Module              | Linker module name                                     |
2707: +=====================+========================================================+
2708: | Base prelude        | `py` (reserved)                                        |
2709: +---------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
2710: | Hook prelude        | `pysp` (reserved)                                      |
2711: +---------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
2712: | Python module       | `pym.a$b$c`; `$` is valid EDN and never in a Python    |
2713: | `a.b.c`             | identifier, so the mapping is injective. The original  |
2714: |                     | Python name stays in module metadata. Nothing is ever  |
2715: |                     | installed at the `pym` root.                           |
2716: +---------------------+--------------------------------------------------------+
2717: ```
2718: 
2719: The registry-prefix defect is filed with the linker seat, with tests for
2720: both installation orders.
2721: 
2722: Resolution, in order:
2723: 
2724: 1. `sys.modules`, a heap dict in prelude state; a hit returns the module
2725:    object.
2726: 2. Runtime-synthesized modules, `sys` and `builtins`, pre-seeded by
2727:    `py/init!`.
2728: 3. The linker: a task registry hit, else name environment, manifest,
2729:    verify, pure install, receive.
2730: 4. Refusal (see catchable imports below).
2731: 
2732: There is no `sys.path` and there are no finders; the search path is the
2733: reader's snapshot set and declared principals, and a dependency edge
2734: names a content address (section 9.6).
2735: 
2736: `py/import`, prelude code, on a miss creates the module object, sets
2737: `__name__` and `__package__`, inserts it into `sys.modules` before
2738: running the body, and runs the body; on an exception it removes the entry
2739: and re-raises. `py/run-main` instantiates the same code image as
2740: `"__main__"`, so the code address does not depend on the role and
2741: `if __name__ == '__main__'` needs nothing else. `__file__` is absent;
2742: `__spec__` and `__loader__` are `None`.

2744: The module store does not back the namespace:
2745: 
2746: - The module store holds `spec` and `body`, immutable after install.
2747: - The module object is a heap cell `{:py/type :module :name s :dict d}`,
2748:   where `d` is the dict the body receives as `%globals`.
2749: - `setattr`, `del`, and `globals()` writes are heap dict operations; the
2750:   linker's store model (literal keys, no delete, first link wins) is
2751:   untouched.
2752: - Two tasks importing one module get independent namespaces, one Python
2753:   process being one task. The linker's open cross-task module-store
2754:   decision is not needed, and module state migrates only when heap lift
2755:   lands.
2756: 
2757: Builtins (ruling 2). `py/init!` builds one builtin namespace dict per
2758: Python task, shared by that task's modules. A global lookup checks the
2759: module namespace, then falls back to the builtins, Python's own model, at
2760: the cost of a second lookup on a global miss. Interpreter-generated
2761: exceptions keep canonical builtin class references even when guest code
2762: rebinds the name. Tests cover initialization twice, builtin mutation,
2763: global shadow and delete, and cross-module exception identity.
2764: 
2765: Import forms:
2766: 
2767: ```text
2768: +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+
2769: | Form                      | C4 treatment                                     |
2770: +===========================+==================================================+
2771: | `import a.b.c`            | Imports `a`, `a.b`, `a.b.c` in order, each body  |
2772: |                           | once, and sets each as an attribute of its       |
2773: |                           | parent (ruling 13).                              |
2774: +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+
2775: | `from pkg import name`    | Succeeds when `pkg` already exposes the          |
2776: |                           | attribute. Raises only when lookup fails and the |
2777: |                           | unsupported submodule auto-import would be       |
2778: |                           | needed (ruling 13).                              |
2779: +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+
2780: | `from m import *`         | Respects `__all__`; without it, excludes         |
2781: |                           | underscore-prefixed names. Copying every key is  |
2782: |                           | insufficient (ruling 13).                        |
2783: +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+
2784: | Relative imports          | Resolved statically at lowering from the         |
2785: |                           | declared module name and package status:         |
2786: |                           | package `a.b` and module `a.b` have different    |
2787: |                           | bases. A packageless or beyond-top-level case    |
2788: |                           | raises `ImportError` at the executed statement.  |
2789: |                           | Rebinding `__package__` or a different runtime   |
2790: |                           | package does not retarget them, a disclosed      |
2791: |                           | restriction (ruling 12).                         |
2792: +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+
2793: | `importlib.import_module` | Only statically recognized calls with a literal  |
2794: |                           | name; dynamic forms get an explicit diagnostic.  |
2795: |                           | Rebinding or aliasing `import_module` must not   |
2796: |                           | make the compiler recognize the wrong callable   |
2797: |                           | (ruling 10).                                     |
2798: +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+
2799: | `importlib.reload`        | Re-runs the same image against the same dict;    |
2800: |                           | the module object and dict are retained, names   |
2801: |                           | not overwritten survive, external bindings are   |
2802: |                           | unchanged, and a failure propagates without      |
2803: |                           | being treated as a failed first import (ruling   |
2804: |                           | 11).                                             |
2805: +---------------------------+--------------------------------------------------+
2806: | Finders, loaders,         | Refused with an explicit unsupported error       |
2807: | `meta_path`,              | (ruling 11).                                     |

2815: interpret computed names against an immutable catalog. Reload cannot
